newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says Q1 internal public debt rises.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says Q1 internal public debt rises.

text.p: Mexico's gross internal public debt was 205.979 billion pesos at the end of the first quarter, 13.817 billion pesos higher than at the end of 1996, the Finance Ministry said in a report released on Thursday.

The increase was due to an increase in net debt of 9.663 billion pesos, a series of adjustments on the inflation-indexed debt for 4.359 billion pesos and an adjustment in the figures that the federal government for a value of 204 million pesos.

The structure of the gross internal debt at the end of the first quarter was Bondes, 35.7 percent; Cetes, 27.8 percent; Ajustabonos, 10.3 percent; the Retirement Savings System, 19.3 percent; Udibonos, 5.9 percent; and other, 1.0 percent, it said.

The average term of government paper placed with the saving public was 336 days at the end of March, compared with 305 days by the last week of 1996. The increase in average terms is a 66.3 percent rise compared with the average term at the end of 1994.
"This has been due to the stability observed in financial markets, which has caused a greater demand for long-term securities," the ministry said.
Mexico's external public debt fell by $4.353 billion to $93.931 billion at the end of the first quarter from the end of 1996, it also said.
The cost of servicing the external public debt rose to $11.259 billion in the first quarter.
Of that amount, $9.459 billion corresponded to amortization of principal, $1.80 billion to the financial cost of the debt, including interest, commissions and expenses, it said.
